The limiter updates this value (for example in Update(int, double, double, VsyncMode) and ChangeSettings(Settings)) and it is clamped to the configured Limit. Not thread-safe — intended to be used from the main/update thread. Methods ChangeSettings(Settings) Applies the provided AdaptiveFpsLimiter.Settings to the limiter. Updates limits, enabled state and all related configuration properties, clamps the current target FPS to the new limit and resets internal runtime state. public bool ChangeSettings(AdaptiveFpsLimiter.Settings newSettings) Parameters newSettings AdaptiveFpsLimiter.Settings The new settings to apply. Returns bool True if the settings were applied successfully. SetEnabled(bool) Enables or disables the adaptive FPS limiter. public void SetEnabled(bool enabled) Parameters enabled bool True to enable the limiter; false to disable. When disabling, the limiter's internal runtime state is reset. Calling with the current value is a no-op. Remarks This method is intended to be called from the engine's main/update thread and is not thread-safe.

MaxDeltaTime Maximum allowed delta time (in seconds) for a single frame. public double MaxDeltaTime { get; } Property Value double Remarks This value is used to clamp the frame delta to avoid very large time steps (which can destabilize physics or cause large logic jumps) when the application experiences a hitch or is resumed after being suspended. MaxDynamicSubsteps Maximum number of dynamic substeps allowed when dynamic substepping is active. MaxDynamicTimestep Maximum dynamic timestep used when performing dynamic substepping. public double MaxDynamicTimestep { get; } Property Value double Remarks Represents the largest allowed duration (in seconds) for an individual dynamic substep when splitting a large frame delta into multiple updates. api/ShapeEngine.Core.Structs.FramerateSe.summary: Struct FramerateSettings Namespace ShapeEngine.Core.Structs Assembly ShapeEngine.dll Represents immutable framerate configuration used by the engine. Contains global and context-specific frame rate limits (focused, unfocused, idle), fixed-update framerate, adaptive FPS limiter settings, delta-time constraints and dynamic substepping parameters. Designed as a value type for inexpensive copies. public readonly struct FramerateSettings Inherited Members ValueType.Equals(object) ValueType.GetHashCode() ValueType.ToString() object.Equals(object, object) object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Extension Methods ShapeLogger.Log(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogConsole(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogFile(object, string, LogLevel) Constructors FramerateSettings(int, int, int, int, int, int, float, Settings, double, int, int) Initializes a new FramerateSettings instance with the specified values. Values are validated and clamped where appropriate. public FramerateSettings(int frameRateLimit, int fixedFramerate, int minFrameRate, int maxFrameRate, int unfocusedFrameRateLimit, int idleFrameRateLimit, float idleTimeThreshold, AdaptiveFpsLimiter.Settings adaptiveFpsLimiterSettings, double maxDeltaTime = 0.2, int minDynamicSubsteppingFramerate = 30, int maxDynamicSubsteps = 6) Parameters frameRateLimit int Global frame rate limit. 0 or less means unlimited; clamped to minFrameRate / maxFrameRate when those bounds are set. fixedFramerate int Fixed update framerate. 0 or less disables fixed-timestep; otherwise clamped to bounds. minFrameRate int Minimum allowed frame rate bound. Set to 0 to disable the lower bound. maxFrameRate int Maximum allowed frame rate bound. Set to 0 to disable the upper bound. unfocusedFrameRateLimit int Frame rate limit applied when the application is unfocused. 0 or less disables the unfocused-specific limit; clamped to bounds when set. idleFrameRateLimit int Frame rate limit applied when the application is idle. 0 or less disables the idle-specific limit. idleTimeThreshold float Seconds without input after which the application is considered idle. 0 or less disables idle detection. adaptiveFpsLimiterSettings AdaptiveFpsLimiter.Settings Settings for the adaptive FPS limiter. maxDeltaTime double Maximum allowed delta time (seconds) for a single frame. Defaults to 0.25. minDynamicSubsteppingFramerate int Minimum allowed target framerate (in frames per second) used for dynamic substepping. maxDynamicSubsteps int Maximum number of dynamic substeps allowed when dynamic substepping is active. Setting this to 0 disables dynamic substepping. Fields AdaptiveFpsLimiterSettings Settings for the adaptive FPS limiter which dynamically adjusts the frame cap. Contains minimum and maximum target frame rates and whether adaptive limiting is enabled. public readonly AdaptiveFpsLimiter.Settings AdaptiveFpsLimiterSettings Field Value AdaptiveFpsLimiter.Settings FixedFramerate Fixed update framerate (in frames per second) used for a fixed-timestep update loop. A value of 0 disables fixed-timestep updates. When enabled the constructor will clamp this value to MinFrameRate / MaxFrameRate if those bounds are active. public readonly int FixedFramerate Field Value int Remarks A fixed frame rate guarantees consistent update intervals regardless of rendering performance. The fixed framerate is not affected by IdleFrameRateLimit or UnfocusedFrameRateLimit. FrameRateLimit The target frame rate limit for the application. 0 or less means unlimited frame rate. public readonly int FrameRateLimit Field Value int IdleFrameRateLimit The target frame rate limit applied when the application is idle (no input detected for IdleTimeThreshold seconds). Set to 0 or less to disable the idle-specific limit (no change from the normal limit). public readonly int IdleFrameRateLimit Field Value int Remarks Use this to reduce CPU/GPU usage while the window does not have focus. IdleTimeThreshold Time in seconds without input after which the application is considered idle. When the idle period is reached the IdleFrameRateLimit may be applied. Set to 0 or less to disable idle detection. public readonly float IdleTimeThreshold Field Value float MaxDeltaTime Maximum allowed delta time (in seconds) for a single frame update. The frame delta will be clamped to this value to avoid very large time steps, prevent a spiral of death when fixed framerate is used, and to limit how many substeps the engine may perform in a single frame. public readonly double MaxDeltaTime Field Value double MaxDynamicSubsteps Maximum number of dynamic substeps allowed when dynamic substepping is active. Limits how many smaller update steps the engine may perform in a single frame to smooth out large frame deltas. Clamped to be non-negative in the constructor; a value of 0 effectively disables dynamic substepping. public readonly int MaxDynamicSubsteps Field Value int Remarks The engine will reduce the allowed substeps every consecutive frame where substepping was performed to avoid spiraling. Frames without substepping increase the allowed substeps back up to this maximum. MaxFrameRate Maximum allowed frame rate used to constrain other framerate-related settings. Applies as the upper bound for the adaptive FPS limiter. When no explicit frame rate limit is set, this value is used as the effective cap. Set to 0 to disable the upper bound. public readonly int MaxFrameRate Field Value int MinDynamicSubsteppingFramerate Minimum allowed target framerate (in frames per second) used when dynamic substepping is active. This value constrains how low the effective framerate may go when splitting a large frame delta into multiple substeps. Clamped to be non-negative in the constructor. Set to 0 to disable the lower bound. public readonly int MinDynamicSubsteppingFramerate Field Value int Remarks When dynamic substepping is enabled, this value effectively guarantees the maximum delta the update loop can receive. Even when the delta time explodes to very high values, the worst case scenario is 1 substep per frame with a delta of 1 / MinDynamicSubsteppingFramerate seconds. MinFrameRate Minimum allowed frame rate used to constrain other framerate-related settings. Applies as the lower bound for the adaptive FPS limiter. Clamps the fixed framerate when enabled. Clamps any explicit frame rate limit when enabled. Set to 0 to disable the lower bound. public readonly int MinFrameRate Field Value int UnfocusedFrameRateLimit The target frame rate limit applied when the application window is unfocused. Set to 0 or less to disable the unfocused-specific limit (no change from the normal limit). public readonly int UnfocusedFrameRateLimit Field Value int Remarks Use this to reduce CPU/GPU usage while the window does not have focus. Properties Default Default framerate settings used by the engine. Provides sensible defaults for normal (non-fixed) operation: Target frame rate limit of 60. Fixed framerate disabled (0 = disabled). Min frame rate of 30. Max frame rate of 120. Unfocused frame rate limit of 30. Idle frame rate limit of 30 after 120 seconds of inactivity. Adaptive FPS limiter enabled with default settings. Default Max delta time of 0.25 seconds. Dynamic substepping enabled with a minimum framerate of 30 and a maximum of 6 substeps. public static FramerateSettings Default { get; } Property Value FramerateSettings Remarks Immutable convenience instance intended for initialization when no user configuration is provided. DefaultFixed Predefined framerate settings configured for fixed-timestep operation. Target frame rate limit: 60 Fixed framerate (enabled): 60 Min/Max frame rate bounds: 30 / 60 Unfocused and idle limits: 30 FPS (idle applied after 120s) Adaptive FPS limiter: disabled Max delta time: 0.16s Dynamic substepping: disabled public static FramerateSettings DefaultFixed { get; } Property Value FramerateSettings Unlimited Predefined framerate settings representing an "unlimited" configuration. No explicit global frame rate cap (FrameRateLimit = 0 -> unlimited). Fixed framerate disabled (FixedFramerate = 0). No minimum or maximum bounds applied (MinFrameRate = 0, MaxFrameRate = 0). Unfocused (30Fps) and idle (30Fps/120s) limits remain enabled to reduce background CPU/GPU usage. Adaptive FPS limiter disabled. Max delta time of 0.25 seconds. Dynamic substepping enabled with a minimum framerate of 30 and a maximum of 6 substeps. public static FramerateSettings Unlimited { get; } Property Value FramerateSettings UnlimitedAdaptive Predefined framerate settings for an "unlimited adaptive" configuration: No explicit global frame rate cap (FrameRateLimit = 0 -> unlimited). Fixed framerate disabled (FixedFramerate = 0). No minimum bound (MinFrameRate = 0) and a high MaxFrameRate to allow adaptive behavior. Unfocused (30Fps) and idle (30Fps/120s) limits remain enabled to reduce background CPU/GPU usage. Adaptive FPS limiter enabled with default settings. Max delta time of 0.25 seconds Dynamic substepping enabled with a minimum framerate of 30 and a maximum of 6 substeps. public static FramerateSettings UnlimitedAdaptive { get; } Property Value FramerateSettings

api/ShapeEngine.Core.TriangleBatch.html.summary: Class TriangleBatch Namespace ShapeEngine.Core Assembly ShapeEngine.dll A class for efficient triangle drawing using Raylib's RLGL, supporting both persistent batches and immediate-mode drawing. This class serves two main purposes: Pooled Instances: obtain an instance via Get(ColorRgba, int) to manage a persistent list of vertices. This is ideal for static geometry that doesn't change often. The batch can be drawn repeatedly with Draw(). Remember to return it to the pool with Return(TriangleBatch) when finished. Immediate Mode (Static): use static methods like StartImmediateBatch(ColorRgba), AddImmediateVertex(float, float), and EndImmediateBatch() for dynamic, per-frame triangle drawing without managing a specific object instance. Both approaches utilize Raylib_cs.DrawMode.Triangles, meaning every 3 consecutive vertices form a single triangle. public class TriangleBatch Inheritance object TriangleBatch Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Extension Methods ShapeLogger.Log(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogConsole(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogFile(object, string, LogLevel) Properties InUse Gets a value indicating whether this batch is currently in use. public bool InUse { get; } Property Value bool Methods AddImmediateTriangle(Triangle) Adds a triangle's vertices to the current batch. public static void AddImmediateTriangle(Triangle triangle) Parameters triangle Triangle The triangle to add. Remarks Batch must be active before using this function. Use StartImmediateBatch(ColorRgba) to start a batch before setting the color. AddImmediateTriangle(Triangle, ColorRgba) Sets the color and adds a triangle's vertices to the current batch. The color used will affect all subsequent vertices until changed again or the batch ends. public static void AddImmediateTriangle(Triangle triangle, ColorRgba color) Parameters triangle Triangle The triangle to add. color ColorRgba The color to use for this triangle. Remarks Batch must be active before using this function. Use StartImmediateBatch(ColorRgba) to start a batch before setting the color. api/ShapeEngine.Geometry.CellCollision.C.title: Class CellCollisionSystem | ShapeEngine
api/ShapeEngine.Geometry.CellCollision.C.summary: Class CellCollisionSystem Namespace ShapeEngine.Geometry.CellCollision Assembly ShapeEngine.dll Cell-based collision system that partitions world space into a grid of cells of the specified size. Manages registration of ICellCollider instances, updates their positions each frame, moves them between cells, and invokes enter/exit and collision start/end callbacks accordingly. public class CellCollisionSystem Inheritance object CellCollisionSystem Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Extension Methods ShapeLogger.Log(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogConsole(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogFile(object, string, LogLevel) Constructors CellCollisionSystem(Size) Cell-based collision system that partitions world space into a grid of cells of the specified size. Manages registration of ICellCollider instances, updates their positions each frame, moves them between cells, and invokes enter/exit and collision start/end callbacks accordingly. public CellCollisionSystem(Size cellSize) Parameters cellSize Size Size of each grid cell in world units (width and height). Methods Add(ICellCollider) Request registration of a collider with the cell collision system. If the collider is currently scheduled for removal this frame, the add will be rejected. The collider is enqueued and will be processed by ShapeEngine.Geometry.CellCollision.CellCollisionSystem.ProcessPendingColliders() on the next update. public bool Add(ICellCollider collider) Parameters collider ICellCollider The ICellCollider to add. Returns bool True if the collider was successfully queued for addition; false if it was already scheduled for removal or already present in the add queue. Clear() Clears the collision system state and returns all pooled resources. public void Clear() Remarks This method clears the pending add/remove queues, unregisters all colliders, and returns any allocated pooled CellCollisionSystem.Cell instances back to the pool. After calling Clear(), the system will be in an empty state with no registered colliders or active cells. Close() Closes the collision system and releases any managed resources. public void Close() Remarks This currently delegates to Clear() to unregister colliders and return pooled cell instances. DrawDebug(ColorRgba, ColorRgba, ColorRgba) Draws a debug visualization of the collision grid. Renders grid lines for all tracked cells, optionally fills occupied cells, and draws an outer bounding rectangle around the active cell area. public void DrawDebug(ColorRgba lineColor, ColorRgba fillColor, ColorRgba borderColor) Parameters lineColor ColorRgba Color used to draw the grid lines for each cell. fillColor ColorRgba Color used to fill cells that contain occupants. borderColor ColorRgba Color used to draw the bounding rectangle around all active cells. GetAllColliders<T>(ref HashSet<T>) Copies all registered colliders of type T into the provided result set. Iterates the internal registry and adds any collider that can be cast to T. public int GetAllColliders<T>(ref HashSet<T> result) where T : ICellCollider Parameters result HashSet<T> A reference to a HashSet<T> that will be populated with matching colliders. The set is modified in-place; duplicates are ignored. Returns int The number of colliders added to result by this call. Type Parameters T The collider concrete type to filter for. Must implement ICellCollider. Remove(ICellCollider) Schedule a collider to be unregistered from the collision system. If the collider is currently queued for addition this frame, it will be removed from the add queue. The actual removal will be processed by ShapeEngine.Geometry.CellCollision.CellCollisionSystem.ProcessPendingColliders() on the next update, which will call RemoveCollider(ICellCollider) to perform the removal and trigger any necessary exit/collision end callbacks. public bool Remove(ICellCollider collider) Parameters collider ICellCollider The ICellCollider instance to remove. Returns bool True if the collider was successfully queued for removal (i.e. added to the internal removal set); false if it was already present in the removal queue. Update(float) Advance the collision system by a single frame. This will process any pending additions/removals, update all registered colliders' positions by dt, and resolve collisions for colliders that moved between cells during this update. public void Update(float dt) Parameters dt float Delta time in seconds since the last update.

api/ShapeEngine.Geometry.CellCollision.h.title: Namespace ShapeEngine.Geometry.CellCollision | ShapeEngine
api/ShapeEngine.Geometry.CellCollision.h.summary: Namespace ShapeEngine.Geometry.CellCollision Classes CellCollisionSystem Cell-based collision system that partitions world space into a grid of cells of the specified size. Manages registration of ICellCollider instances, updates their positions each frame, moves them between cells, and invokes enter/exit and collision start/end callbacks accordingly. Interfaces ICellCollider Represents an object that can participate in the cell-based collision system. Implementers are queried for position, collision layer/mask and receive lifecycle callbacks when they enter/exit cells or start/end collisions with other colliders.

api/ShapeEngine.Geometry.CollisionSystem.summary: Class BroadphaseDynamicSpatialHash Namespace ShapeEngine.Geometry.CollisionSystem Assembly ShapeEngine.dll Implements a dynamic spatial hash broadphase for collision detection. Efficiently manages colliders in spatial buckets for fast broadphase queries. Only creates and stores buckets that contain colliders, optimizing memory usage. Old buckets that become empty are recycled for future use. The bounding box is used for broadphase checks, but not the full shape. This is not recommended for very large objects. Especially large thin objects, like lines, segments, or rays. FullShape = 2 Suited for large or complicated objects where precise querying is needed. The full shape is used for broadphase checks, which can be more computationally intensive, but shape is only placed in necessary buckets. Point = 0 Optimized for very small objects. Only a point is used for broadphase checks.

api/ShapeEngine.Geometry.CollisionSystem.summary: Namespace ShapeEngine.Geometry.CollisionSystem Classes BroadphaseBucket Represents a collection of colliders within a single spatial hash bucket. BroadphaseColliderRegister<T> Manages a register of colliders and their associated data for broadphase collision detection. BroadphaseDynamicSpatialHash Implements a dynamic spatial hash broadphase for collision detection. Efficiently manages colliders in spatial buckets for fast broadphase queries. Only creates and stores buckets that contain colliders, optimizing memory usage. Old buckets that become empty are recycled for future use. Does not maintain persistent bounds; bounds are recalculated each frame based on added colliders. BroadphaseSpatialHash Implements a spatial hash grid for efficient broad-phase collision detection and spatial queries. BroadphaseStaticColliderRegister<T> Manages registration and tracking of static colliders and their associated data for broadphase collision detection. CastSpaceEntry Represents a collection of colliders associated with a specific collision object, used for cast space queries. CastSpaceResult Represents the result of a cast space query, mapping collision objects to their associated colliders. Collider Abstract base class for all colliders in the collision system. Collision Contains the information of an intersection or an overlap between two colliders. CollisionInformation Contains the information of a collision between two collision objects in the form of a list of collisions. Each collision is an intersection or overlap between two colliders. CollisionObject Represents an object that participates in the collision system and can contain multiple colliders. Handles collision detection, intersection, and overlap logic, and provides events and hooks for collision notifications. IntersectSpaceEntry Represents an entry in the intersection space, containing collision points and information about the other collider involved in the intersection. IntersectSpaceRegister Represents a register of intersection entries for a specific CollisionObject. IntersectSpaceResult Represents the result of an intersection space query, containing registers of intersection entries for multiple collision objects. IntersectionPoints Represents a list of IntersectionPoints, providing validation, filtering, and sorting utilities for collision detection. Overlap Represents an overlap between two colliders. Structs ClosestPointResult Represents the result of a closest point calculation between two shapes or segments, including the points, distance, and segment indices. CollisionPointValidationResult Represents the result of validating collision points, containing various relevant points. IntersectionPoint Represents a single intersection point, including its position and normal vector. Interfaces IBroadphase Represents a broadphase collision detection system interface. Inherits from IBounds. Provides methods for managing collision objects and retrieving candidate buckets for collision checks. Use FixWindingOrder() or MakeCounterClockwise() if your points are in clockwise (CW) order. A convex polygon is a polygon where all interior angles are less than 180°, and every line segment between any two points inside the polygon lies entirely within the polygon. In other words, no vertices "point inward." A concave polygon is a polygon that has at least one interior angle greater than 180°, and at least one line segment between points inside the polygon passes outside the polygon. This means it has at least one "caved-in" or inward-pointing vertex. api/ShapeEngine.Input.InputSystem.html.summary: Class InputSystem Namespace ShapeEngine.Input Assembly ShapeEngine.dll Represents the main input system for managing input devices, input actions, and access control. Handles device updates, action trees, and provides locking mechanisms for input processing. public sealed class InputSystem Inheritance object InputSystem Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Extension Methods ShapeLogger.Log(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogConsole(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogFile(object, string, LogLevel) Fields ActiveInputActionTreeGroup A global collection of InputActionTree instances. Each tree manages a hierarchy of input actions and their bindings. public readonly InputActionTreeGroup ActiveInputActionTreeGroup Field Value InputActionTreeGroup AllAccessTag This access tag grants access regardless of the input system lock. public const uint AllAccessTag = 1 Field Value uint DefaultAccessTag The default access tag for actions. public const uint DefaultAccessTag = 2 Field Value uint Properties CurrentInputActionDeviceType Current InputAction based device type detected by ActiveInputActionTreeGroup. The first non-None InputDeviceType detected during the update of the ActiveInputActionTreeGroup is used. public InputDeviceType CurrentInputActionDeviceType { get; } Property Value InputDeviceType Remarks For an InputActions IInputTypes InputDeviceType to be considered the following conditions must be met: The InputAction must be part of an InputActionTree within the ActiveInputActionTreeGroup. The InputAction must be active. The IInputType's InputState must be down. The IInputType must not be blocked (when BlocksInput is true). CurrentInputDeviceType Gets the current input device type in use. public InputDeviceType CurrentInputDeviceType { get; } Property Value InputDeviceType CurrentInputDeviceTypeNoMouse Gets the current input device type, but returns Keyboard if Mouse is active. public InputDeviceType CurrentInputDeviceTypeNoMouse { get; } Property Value InputDeviceType GamepadManager The global gamepad device manager instance. public GamepadDeviceManager GamepadManager { get; } Property Value GamepadDeviceManager InputActionDeviceSelectionCooldownActive Indicates whether the input action device selection cooldown is currently active. Returns true if the cooldown timer is greater than zero. public bool InputActionDeviceSelectionCooldownActive { get; } Property Value bool InputDeviceSelectionCooldownActive Indicates whether the input device selection cooldown is currently active. Returns true if the cooldown timer is greater than zero. public bool InputDeviceSelectionCooldownActive { get; } Property Value bool InputSettings Gets the current input settings. public InputSettings InputSettings { get; } Property Value InputSettings InputUsed public bool InputUsed { get; } Property Value bool Keyboard The global keyboard device instance. public KeyboardDevice Keyboard { get; } Property Value KeyboardDevice Locked Indicates if the input system is currently locked. When set to true, InputActions and other input requests will only be processed if they have the AllAccessTag or their access tag is contained in the lock whitelist. All InputActions and input request with an access tag contained in the lock blacklist will not be processed. public static bool Locked { get; } Property Value bool Mouse The global mouse device instance. public MouseDevice Mouse { get; } Property Value MouseDevice NextAccessTag Gets the next available access tag. 1 is reserved for AllAccessTag, 2 is reserved for DefaultAccessTag. Only power of 2 values are used for access tags. public static uint NextAccessTag { get; } Property Value uint Methods ApplyInputDeviceChangeSettings(InputSettings) Applies the InputSettings to all attached input devices. public void ApplyInputDeviceChangeSettings(InputSettings settings) Parameters settings InputSettings The new InputSettings to apply. Remarks Settings are applied to Mouse, Keyboard, and GamepadManager that applies the settings to all GamepadDevices. HasAccess(InputAction) Determines if the specified action has access. public static bool HasAccess(InputAction action) Parameters action InputAction The input action to check. Returns bool True if access is granted; otherwise, false. HasAccess(uint) Determines if the specified access tag has access. AllAccessTag always returns true (has access). If tag is contained in the current blacklist, this function will return false (no access). If tag is not contained in the current blacklist and tag is contained in the current whitelist, or the current whitelist is empty, this function will return true (has access). public static bool HasAccess(uint tag) Parameters tag uint The access tag to check. Returns bool True if access is granted; otherwise, false. IsInputAvailable(uint) Determines if input is available for the specified access tag. Always returns true if Locked is false. Otherwise returns HasAccess(uint) with the tag parameter. public static bool IsInputAvailable(uint tag) Parameters tag uint The access tag to check. Returns bool True if input is available; otherwise, false. Lock() Locks the input system, clearing all whitelists and blacklists. Only InputActions and input requests with AllAccessTag will be processed. public static void Lock() Lock(BitFlag, BitFlag) Locks the input system with a specific whitelist and blacklist. All InputActions and other input requests with a tag contained in the whitelist or with the AllAccessTag will be processed. All InputActions and other input requests with a tag contained in the blacklist will not be processed. public static void Lock(BitFlag whitelist, BitFlag blacklist) Parameters whitelist BitFlag The whitelist of access tags. blacklist BitFlag The blacklist of access tags. LockBlacklist(BitFlag) Locks the input system with a specific blacklist. All InputActions and other input requests with a tag contained in the blacklist will not be processed. public static void LockBlacklist(BitFlag blacklist) Parameters blacklist BitFlag The blacklist of access tags. LockWhitelist(BitFlag) Locks the input system with a specific whitelist. All InputActions and other input requests with a tag contained in the whitelist or with the AllAccessTag will be processed. public static void LockWhitelist(BitFlag whitelist) Parameters whitelist BitFlag The whitelist of access tags. Unlock() Unlocks the input system, clearing all whitelists and blacklists. public static void Unlock() Events OnInputActionDeviceTypeChanged Event triggered when CurrentInputActionDeviceType changes. public event Action<InputDeviceType, InputDeviceType>? However, gamepad-related modifier keys only function with gamepad-related input. For example, while "[Shift] + Right Bumper" is technically valid, the order and context matter: "[Right Bumper] + Shift" does not work because gamepad modifiers require a gamepad input context. Combinations like "[Shift] + Left Mouse Button" or "[Middle Mouse Button] + Space" are valid, as they involve keyboard or mouse modifiers. Always ensure that gamepad modifiers are paired with gamepad inputs for correct behavior. So you can pair any modifier type with gamepad input, but gamepad modifiers will only work with gamepad input. Remarks This class is used to define combinations of modifier keys (like Shift, Ctrl, Alt) that must be active for an input to be triggered. The keys can be combined using either an AND or an OR logic. api/ShapeEngine.Pathfinding.NodeCostType.summary: Enum NodeCostType Namespace ShapeEngine.Pathfinding Assembly ShapeEngine.dll Enumerates the types of node value operations that can be applied to a node. public enum NodeCostType Extension Methods ShapeLogger.Log(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogConsole(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogFile(object, string, LogLevel) Fields AddBonus = 6 Adds a bonus value to the node. (multiplicative cost, -3 would be 1/4 of the cost, +3 would be 4x the cost) AddFlat = 9 Adds a flat value to the node. Block = 3 Blocks the node, making it impassable. None = -1 No operation; the node value remains unchanged. RemoveBonus = 7 Removes a bonus value from the node. (multiplicative cost, -3 would be 1/4 of the cost, +3 would be 4x the cost) RemoveFlat = 10 Removes a flat value from the node. Reset = 0 Resets the node to its default value. ResetBonus = 8 Resets the bonus value of the node. ResetFlat = 11 Resets the flat value of the node. ResetThenBlock = 5 Resets the node and then blocks it. ResetThenSetBaseValue = 2 Resets the node and then sets it to a specific value. SetBaseValue = 1 Sets the node to a specific value. Unblock = 4 Unblocks the node, making it passable.

Useful for scenarios where you need to randomly select indices with custom likelihoods. The ChanceList system guarantees that each index is picked according to its weight until all indices are exhausted, at which point the list can be refilled. (An index with weight 10 out of a total weight of 100 will have been picked exactly 10 times after 100 picks.) If used for XML serialization, XML attributes have to be used and added to Name and SpawnWeight members using new keyword (see XML code example). DataObjectDict<T> Represents a dictionary of T objects, providing advanced random selection and filtering capabilities. DataObjectList<T> Represents a strongly-typed list of T objects, where T is a subclass of DataObject. Provides methods for retrieving entries by name and for selecting random entries, including type-specific and unique selections. JsonClassSerializer<T> Provides serialization and deserialization of objects to and from JSON using customizable options. JsonDataObjectSerializer<T> Provides serialization and deserialization functionality for T objects using System.Text.Json. JsonStructSerializer<T> Provides serialization and deserialization of value types (structs) to and from JSON using customizable options. XmlClassSerializer<T> Provides XML serialization and deserialization for reference types using XmlSerializer. XmlDataObjectSerializer<T> Provides XML serialization and deserialization for objects of type T. T must inherit from DataObject and should be compatible with XmlSerializer. XmlStructSerializer<T> Provides XML serialization and deserialization for value types (structs) using XmlSerializer. Interfaces ICsvSerializable Interface for objects that can be serialized to and deserialized from CSV format.

api/ShapeEngine.ShapeClipper.ShapeClippe.summary: Enum ShapeClipperEndType Namespace ShapeEngine.ShapeClipper Assembly ShapeEngine.dll The ShapeClipperEndType enumerator controls how the ends of paths are handled when performing offset (inflating/shrinking) operations. This enumeration is only required for offset operations and is not used for polygon clipping. public enum ShapeClipperEndType Extension Methods ShapeClipperConversion2D.ToClipperEndType(ShapeClipperEndType) ShapeClipperConversion2D.ToLineCapType(ShapeClipperEndType) ShapeLogger.Log(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogConsole(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogFile(object, string, LogLevel) Fields Butt = 2 Path ends are squared off without any extension (flat cutoff at ends). Joined = 1 The path is treated as a polyline and its ends are joined during offsetting. (Outline) Polygon = 0 The path is treated as a closed polygon; offsets consider the path closed. (Filled) Round = 4 Path ends are extended by the offset amount and rounded (arc) off. Square = 3 Path ends are extended by the offset amount and then squared off. Remarks With both ShapeClipperEndType.Polygon and ShapeClipperEndType.Joined, path closure will occur regardless of whether or not the first and last vertices in the path match.

api/ShapeEngine.ShapeClipper.ShapeClippe.title: Enum ShapeClipperFillRule | ShapeEngine
api/ShapeEngine.ShapeClipper.ShapeClippe.summary: Enum ShapeClipperFillRule Namespace ShapeEngine.ShapeClipper Assembly ShapeEngine.dll Filling rules determine which sub-regions of complex polygons are considered "inside". Complex polygons are defined by one or more closed contours; only portions of these contours may contribute to filled regions, so a filling rule is required to decide which sub-regions are treated as inside when performing clipping operations. public enum ShapeClipperFillRule Extension Methods ShapeClipperConversion2D.ToClipperFillRule(ShapeClipperFillRule) ShapeLogger.Log(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogConsole(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogFile(object, string, LogLevel) Fields EvenOdd = 0 Even-Odd rule: only sub-regions with odd winding parity are filled. Negative = 3 Negative rule: only sub-regions with winding counts < 0 are filled. NonZero = 1 Non-Zero rule: any sub-region with a non-zero winding number is filled. Positive = 2 Positive rule: only sub-regions with winding counts > 0 are filled. Examples Example algorithm (winding number): From a point outside the polygon draw a ray through the polygon. Start with winding number 0. For each contour crossed, increment the winding number if the crossing goes right-to-left relative to the ray, otherwise decrement. Each sub-region gets the current winding number. Remarks The supported fill rules are based on winding numbers derived from the orientation of each path: Even-Odd: toggles inside/outside each time a contour is crossed. Non-Zero: considers the sum of winding contributions; non-zero means inside. Positive / Negative: depend on the sign of the winding number. Notes: The most commonly used rules are Even-Odd and Non-Zero. Reversing a path reverses its orientation (and the sign of winding numbers) but does not affect parity or whether a winding number is zero. Filling rules are required only for clipping operations; they do not affect polygon offsetting.

api/ShapeEngine.ShapeClipper.ShapeClippe.title: Enum ShapeClipperJoinType | ShapeEngine
api/ShapeEngine.ShapeClipper.ShapeClippe.summary: Enum ShapeClipperJoinType Namespace ShapeEngine.ShapeClipper Assembly ShapeEngine.dll Specifies how convex angled joins are handled when offsetting (inflating/shrinking) paths. This enumeration is only required for offset operations (e.g. ClipperOffset) and is not used for polygon clipping operations. public enum ShapeClipperJoinType Extension Methods ShapeClipperConversion2D.ToClipperJoinType(ShapeClipperJoinType) ShapeLogger.Log(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogConsole(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogFile(object, string, LogLevel) Fields Bevel = 2 Bevel joins cut the corner with a straight edge between the offset edges. Beveling is typically simpler and faster than squared joins and is common in many graphics formats. Miter = 0 Edges are offset a specified distance and extended to their intersection points. A miter limit is enforced to prevent very long spikes at acute angles; when the limit is exceeded the join is converted to a squared/bevel form. Round = 3 Convex joins are rounded using an arc with radius equal to the offset distance and the original join vertex as the arc center. Square = 1 Convex joins are truncated with a squared edge. The midpoint of the squared edge is exactly the offset distance from the original vertex.

ShapeClipper2D Provides shared Clipper-backed 2D geometry utilities and configuration for path extraction, clipping, offsetting, shape creation, simplification, winding analysis, and hole filtering. ShapeClipper64 Provides reusable helpers for performing boolean clipping operations on Clipper Clipper2Lib.Path64 and Clipper2Lib.Paths64 geometry, as well as engine polygon data represented by Vector2 lists. ShapeClipperConversion2D Provides Clipper/world-space conversion helpers for 2D paths, polygons, rectangles, points, and related enums. ShapeClipperDrawing2D Provides immediate-style drawing helpers for polygons and polylines backed by ShapeClipper triangulation. ShapeClipperOffset Wraps a Clipper2Lib.ClipperOffset instance to offset polygons and polylines using the engine's world-space coordinate conventions. ShapeClipperTriangulation2D Provides Clipper-backed triangulation helpers for polygons, polygon outlines, and polyline strokes in 2D. TriMesh Represents a mutable triangle mesh stored as a flat vertex buffer. TriMeshPool Provides a simple reusable pool of TriMesh instances to reduce allocations during repeated triangulation work. Enums ShapeClipperClipType Specifies the boolean clipping operation to apply when combining shapes. ShapeClipperEndType The ShapeClipperEndType enumerator controls how the ends of paths are handled when performing offset (inflating/shrinking) operations. This enumeration is only required for offset operations and is not used for polygon clipping. ShapeClipperFillRule Filling rules determine which sub-regions of complex polygons are considered "inside". Complex polygons are defined by one or more closed contours; only portions of these contours may contribute to filled regions, so a filling rule is required to decide which sub-regions are treated as inside when performing clipping operations. ShapeClipperJoinType Specifies how convex angled joins are handled when offsetting (inflating/shrinking) paths. This enumeration is only required for offset operations (e.g. ClipperOffset) and is not used for polygon clipping operations.

api/ShapeEngine.StaticLib.PerlinNoise2D..summary: Class PerlinNoise2D Namespace ShapeEngine.StaticLib Assembly ShapeEngine.dll Provides 2D Perlin noise generation utilities. Produces smooth, continuous noise values (approximately in the range [-1, 1]) for given world coordinates scaled by a lattice cell size (gridSize). Maintains a static cache of pseudo-random gradient vectors and exposes an integer Seed to change the generated gradients. Changing Seed clears the gradient cache. public static class PerlinNoise2D Inheritance object PerlinNoise2D Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The internal gradient cache is not synchronized; use external synchronization for concurrent access. Properties Seed Gets or sets the integer seed used to generate pseudo-random gradient vectors. Setting a new value clears the cached gradient table so subsequent noise samples use gradients derived from the new seed. public static int Seed { get; set; } Property Value int The seed value. index.html.summary: My custom-made engine based on the great Raylib Framework. The Main focus is being performant and only using draw functions instead of textures. When using Shape Engine everything from Raylib is available as well. (Raylib Examples, Raylib Cheatsheet) Shape Engine´s examples are available on Itch as well and it is a great way to support me ;) More examples are available in the ShapeEngineDemos repository. Most of the bigger examples will be available here, like a small asteroids game. You are free to use Shape Engine or any part of Shape Engine for your own projects, but keep in mind that Shape Engine was designed to help me with my specific game dev needs. Nevertheless I am looking forward to creations that Shape Engine made possible :) Release Trailer Showcase Minimal Project Setup using System.Drawing; using ShapeEngine.Color; using ShapeEngine.Core; using ShapeEngine.Core.Structs; using ShapeEngine.Lib; namespace ShapeEngineProject; public static class Program { public static void Main(string[] args) { var game = new MyGameClass(GameSettings.StretchMode, WindowSettings.Default); game.Run(); } } public class MyGameClass : Game { public MyGameClass(GameSettings gameSettings, WindowSettings windowSettings) : base(gameSettings, windowSettings) { } protected override void DrawGame(ScreenInfo game) { game.Area.Draw(new ColorRgba(Color.DarkOliveGreen)); game.Area.DrawLines(12f, new ColorRgba(Color.AntiqueWhite)); game.MousePos.Draw(24f, new ColorRgba(Color.Lime), 36); } } Development Process The Main Branch contains the current development stage. You can follow the development process here: Reddit Twitter Instagram YouTube GitHub Discussions Roadmap Installation / How to Use There are multiple ways to use Shape Engine: Create a new solution & project and download Shape Engine from the Nuget manager. (Recommended) Clone or fork the repository and add new projects to the solution. You then can reference the Shape Engine project and start working on your game. The advantages are that you can easily change things in Shape Engine and everything updates automatically in your own project. Create a new solution & project in a .net IDE. (Visual Studio / JetBrains Rider for example). Download or fork ShapeEngine and either create a local nuget package or build the solution to create all necessary dll files. [Using a local Nuget Package] Create a folder on your machine called something like “Local Nuget Packages” and copy the ShapeEngine Nuget package that you created to this folder. (You can also add the Shape Engine Nuget package directly to your Project). Now you need to create a new Package source in the Nuget Manager that points to your “Local Nuget Packages” Folder. This source can be used in your Nuget Manager to find and install the Shape Engine Nuget Package. You manually copy all needed DLL files to your project. You need the following DLLs: Clipper2Lib, Raylib-Cs, Microsoft.Toolkit.HighPerformance, Shape Engine Core, Raylib. All DLL files except Raylib can be anywhere in your projects folder hierarchy. The Raylib DLL must be on the root level of your project. You need to select the right Raylib DLL for your operating system. Now just add a reference for all DLLs except the Raylib DLL and you are done. On MacOS you need to do the same step except using the .dylib file instead of the raylib DLL. You need to set the property “Copy if Newer” to true on the .dylib file. Then everything should work. Create a new solution & project and just add the Shape Engine Core DLL to your project and reference it. Now you need to download the right version of the Raylib_CsLo & Clipper2 Nuget packages. The releases on GitHub will state which versions were used. Examples You can download the newest builds of the Example Project on Itch io. You can clone the repo and inspect the example projects there as well. Examples are simple scenes that focus on one specific area or feature of Shape Engine. Examples showcase the various capabilities of Shape Engine, allowing users to explore various features. The examples cover all major features of Shape Engine, ensuring that users can grasp its full potential. Features In general my goal is to provide the most relevant system a game dev needs without adding a solution for every possible problem. Polygon Fracturing Delaunay Triangulation Text & Font System Pathfinding UI System Collision System Audio & Music Savegame System Color Palettes Input System (Keyboard, Mouse, Gamepad) Camera System Screen Texture System Gapped Drawing Documentation & Getting Started Right now there is not much information about how to use Shape Engine. The repository contains an Examples Project. It shows you a lot of what is possible and how it is done and should help you until there is some proper documentation. Currently I don't have the time or the resources to create proper documentation for Shape Engine. If enough people are interested in it this might change. Any help in this direction would be greatly appreciated! Roadmap You can find the roadmap and current milestone of ShapeEngine here. Dependencies I am just using the Raylib Cs c# bindings and the Cipper2 library for polygon clipping. If you use the nuget manager to download Shape Engine as a nuget package you don't have to take care of any dependencies, because they will be downloaded automatically. Limitations There is no physics system because I don´t need one and would´t know how to make one. There is complete collision system but the collision response is up to you. You can also use raylibs physics system. History I made Shape Engine because I wanted to help myself make games with a specific art style and certain limitations. At first, it started out with some helper scripts but now it is a relatively sophisticated system to make games with raylib. Certain parts of the basic game loop are inspired by Bytepath and other things I already used in games that I made myself (especially Fracture Hell). Feel free to use any single part if you don´t want to use the whole package. Contact If you have an issue, or a suggestion for a new feature GitHub is the best way to get in contact with me. GitHub Issues GitHub Discussions On these platforms you can follow the development process of Shape Engine, get in contact with me and always stay up date.
